title: Comparison between Intravitreal Triamcinolone with Grid Laser Photocoagulation versus Bevacizumab with Grid Laser Photocoagulation Combinations for Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion

license.statement: CC BY (article <license>: 'Creative Commons Attribution License'; no version or URL given in the licence element)

groups.agent: intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide 4 mg/0.1 mL plus grid laser photocoagulation
groups.description: Treatment-naive macular edema secondary to branch retinal vein occlusion (edema for less than 3 months at first admission), retrospective (January 2008 to January 2012), 52 eyes of 52 patients: one intravitreal triamcinolone injection, grid laser one month later, monthly follow-up with as-needed reinjection at 4-month intervals and additional laser at 4-month intervals.

groups.agent: intravitreal bevacizumab 1.25 mg/0.05 mL plus grid laser photocoagulation
groups.description: As ivt-glp with intravitreal bevacizumab, 47 eyes of 47 patients: one bevacizumab injection, grid laser one month later, monthly follow-up with as-needed monthly reinjection and additional laser at 4-month intervals.

series.baseline_label: Baseline BCVA (LogMAR) (Table 2, row R2, IVT + GLP column C2)

notes: Unit: BCVA measured with the ETDRS chart at 4 m (Methods 2.2) and converted to logMAR for the analysis (Methods 2.7); Table 2 states LogMAR with no Snellen or decimal row.

Role control for both groups: two standard combination treatments compared retrospectively without a declared experimental arm. Treatment combination: intravitreal drug plus grid laser photocoagulation defines each arm.
Regimen prn: one initial injection, grid laser one month later, then as-needed reinjection by visual acuity loss of one line or more or any CRT increase.
Methods state that ischemic BRVO (5 or more disc areas) was not included, while Table 1 lists ischemic eyes in both groups (text against table; noted only).
The Results text names a 'ranibizumab group' when reporting month-24 proportions, apparently the bevacizumab group; not used.
Central retinal thickness (Table 3), injection counts and complications (Table 4) are reported in the article and mentioned here only.
